findings.F1: The book failed only on Calmar (0.43 against 0.75), and its deepest fall was one stretch in w16 (2020): 19 days, the book down 40.1 % while holding the coins fell 55.6 %. In that window the book's position averaged 0.26, and its coins' 60-day return averaged −17 %.
findings.F2: Inside w16 the strong case still paid: deep falls (≤ −3 %) while 20-day volatility was above 60-day volatility were followed by +1.62 % next day (98 cases). The losses came from the other signal bars: deep falls with falling volatility gave −1.95 % (56 cases), and shallow down days with rising volatility gave −1.49 % (208 cases).
findings.F3: On signal bars the next-day excess return grows with the ratio of 20-day to 60-day volatility, from −0.38 % (t −3.85, 2426 cases) in the lowest fifth to +0.52 % (t 4.50, 2426 cases) in the highest. Taken alone, with no signal, the same highest fifth earns −0.08 % (t −0.69, 2679 cases), so the ratio is no effect of its own.
findings.F4: Deep falls (≤ −3 %) with the volatility ratio at or above 1 give +0.64 % excess next day (t 5.11, 2381 cases). Deep falls with a falling ratio give +0.08 % (t 0.75, 2554 cases). Rising volatility without a deep fall gives −0.01 % (t −0.24, 8316 cases).
findings.F5: The idea's measured size is a total move of +0.20 % per case against a cost of 0.22 % per trade. Only the strong end of the signal clears that cost:
findings.F6: Trading only the bars where the fall is at least 3 % and the volatility ratio is at least 1 changes the failing measure:
findings.F7: Trading only on the volatility ratio at or above 1 lifts Calmar to 0.56 (deepest fall −29.4 %, Sharpe 0.88).
findings.F8: Adding to that condition a close far from its 50-day mean on either side (≤ −16.7 % or ≥ +0.6 %) lifts Calmar to 0.90, with the deepest fall at −19.2 % and Sharpe 1.10.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's percentage fall on its latest day, the more it rises over the next 1 day, and this rebound is larger the higher the coin's volatility over the past 60 days and the more its 20-day volatility exceeds its 60-day volatility.
ideas.consequence: A dip buyer should take the next-day rebound mainly when the fall comes as turbulence is building, and stand aside after falls in calming markets, where the losing days of the deepest drawdowns sit.
ideas.name: volatile falls, rising turbulence rebound

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's percentage fall on its latest day, the more it rises over the next 1 day, larger the higher its 60-day volatility, with the rebound concentrated in the deepest falls, so that the next-day rise grows faster than in proportion to the day's fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader should buy only the deepest falls of a volatile period, where the rebound covers the cost of the trade, rather than every down day.
ideas.name: deepest volatile falls rebound

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's percentage fall on its latest day while its 20-day volatility exceeds its 60-day volatility, the more it rises over the next 1 day, and this rebound is larger the farther the coin's close sits from its 50-day average.
ideas.consequence: A dip buyer should favour stretched coins during building turbulence and expect little after falls near a coin's 50-day average.
ideas.name: stretched turbulent falls rebound
